items.stem: A team needs an LLM assistant to answer from a large, frequently updated internal document set with citations. Which approach fits best?

options.rationale: Correct: RAG retrieves current documents at query time and supports citations without retraining.

options.text: Full fine-tuning on the documents weekly
options.rationale: Frequent full fine-tuning is costly and lags updates versus retrieval.

options.text: A longer system prompt with no retrieval
options.rationale: A static prompt cannot hold or update a large document set.
Temperature controls randomness, not access to documents.

items.explanation: RAG retrieves current documents at query time and supports citations.

items.stem: In a transformer language model, the self-attention mechanism mainly lets the model:

options.text: Weigh the relevance of other tokens when representing each token
options.rationale: Correct: self-attention weights how much each token attends to others.

options.text: Store facts in a lookup database
options.rationale: Transformers do not use an explicit fact database.
Attention is unrelated to code compilation.
Attention does not guarantee factual correctness.

items.explanation: Self-attention weighs the relevance of other tokens for each token.

items.stem: Before deploying an LLM support assistant, select TWO responsible-AI steps that most directly reduce harm.

options.text: Test for biased or unsafe outputs across representative inputs
options.rationale: Correct: red-team/bias testing surfaces harmful behaviour before launch.

options.text: Add guardrails and a human-escalation path for sensitive queries
options.rationale: Correct: guardrails plus escalation limit harm in production.

options.text: Increase the model size to the largest available
options.rationale: A bigger model is not inherently safer.

options.text: Remove all logging to protect privacy
options.rationale: Removing all logging harms monitoring and auditability.

options.text: Raise temperature to make answers more varied
options.rationale: More randomness tends to increase, not reduce, risk.

items.explanation: Bias/safety testing and guardrails with human escalation most directly reduce deployment harm.
